notes: Two readings, kept apart. Each has its own date, its own sample of markets and its own n. They are never added together: there is no combined percentage in this file, because there was never a combined sample.
Every percentage is of `robots_files_read`, not of `domains_requested`. The gap between the two is itself published, under `failures`.
Both readings were parsed by the matcher in `src/index.js` against the token list in `data/ai-crawlers.json`, so anyone with this repository can rebuild either one.
The limitation in `limitations[0]` is not decoration: these are large, high-ranked sites, and the figures are not a picture of small businesses. Quote it with any figure taken from here.

samples.sample: 100 highest-ranked domains per market from the Tranco top-1M list
limitations: These are large, high-ranked sites, not small businesses. Among small businesses the picture is probably different — likely fewer deliberate blocks and more neglect. Do not present these figures as a picture of small businesses.
n = 528 robots.txt files actually read, out of 700 domains requested. Percentages are of the files read, not of the domains requested.
A robots.txt verdict states the request a site is making, not an outcome: some operators document that their agent may ignore robots.txt.

not_sampled.note: Neither was in this sample. The .com figure is the global English-language slice and must not be read as a figure for either country.

samples.sample: 100 highest-ranked domains per market from the Tranco top-1M list, list V354N
limitations: These are large, high-ranked sites, not small businesses. Among small businesses the picture is probably different — likely fewer deliberate blocks and more neglect. Do not present these figures as a picture of small businesses.
n = 350 robots.txt files actually read, out of 500 domains requested. Percentages are of the files read, not of the domains requested.
A site answering 404 on /robots.txt is counted as not read rather than as having no robots.txt. That is the conservative count: it shrinks the denominator and so raises every percentage here.
Korea contributed only 54 read files, the smallest of the five, so the .kr figure moves more than the others.
A robots.txt verdict states the request a site is making, not an outcome: some operators document that their agent may ignore robots.txt.

not_sampled.note: Still not sampled. The .br figure is Brazil and must not be read as a figure for Portugal.
